papers.title: A Novel Solving Method for Multi-Constrained Optimization of Ceramic Composite Armor with Failure Considerations Based on an Improved Response Surface Methodology–Adaptive Moment Estimation (RSM-Adam) Framework
papers.abstract: Optimizing the design of Ceramic Composite Armor Systems (CCASs) is crucial for liberating redundant design space and enhancing ballistic performance. However, existing solution frameworks still exhibit deficiencies in handling multi-constrained optimization, particularly regarding surrogate model generalization and the nonlinearity and non-convexity of solution algorithms, leading to suboptimal accuracy and efficiency. This study proposes a novel Response Surface Methodology–Adaptive Moment Estimation (RSM-Adam) framework to address these challenges. The developed RSM surrogate model integrates key CCAS failure characteristics, such as structural deformation, fiber/matrix failure and interfacial debonding/delamination into the optimization analysis using few finite element analysis (FEA). This approach overcomes the limitation of conventional theoretical models that focus solely on ballistic performance, establishing a foundation for a generalized multi-constrained optimization model. Meanwhile, an improved Adam method incorporating a cosine step-size adjustment strategy demonstrates superior capability in handling nonlinearity and non-convexity during iteration compared to conventional algorithms like the Simulated Annealing Algorithm (SAA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Genetic Algorithm (GA). It achieves over 60% reduction in computational error compared with conventional intelligent algorithms, while maintaining a computational cost comparable to or lower than most of them, proving highly effective and efficient for complex multi-constrained models. The rationality and accuracy of the RSM-Adam framework are validated through ballistic testing and FEA of an Al2O3/Carbon Fiber (CF)/Aramid Fiber (AF) composite armor sample, with systematic analysis of the influence of key framework parameters on optimization outcomes. It is also confirmed that the proposed RSM-Adam framework provides a practical, widely applicable, and engineering-valuable solution for the multi-constrained optimal design of the CCAS.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Smoking is associated with adverse dental implant outcomes, but early smoking-related changes in peri-implant trabecular bone texture remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated longitudinal changes in panoramic radiomics features around dental implants in active smokers and non-smokers. Methods: This retrospective study included 47 patients and 110 implant sites, with 55 implant sites per group. Panoramic radiographs obtained at 0–7 days (T0), 4–6 weeks (T1), and 10–14 weeks (T2) after implant placement were analyzed. Twenty-eight first-order gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) and gray-level run length matrix (GLRLM) features were extracted; features with intraclass correlation coefficients ≥ 0.75 were included in mixed repeated-measures analyses. Results: Twenty-six features met the reliability threshold. Following BH-FDR correction across the 26 group-by-time interaction tests, significant interactions remained for GLCM Contrast (adjusted p = 0.010) and GLRLM Short Run Emphasis (SRE; adjusted p = 0.033). The Entropy interaction did not remain statistically significant after correction (adjusted p = 0.075). Contrast increased in smokers but remained relatively stable in non-smokers, whereas SRE decreased in smokers and increased in non-smokers. Conclusions: Smoking status was associated with divergent early peri-implant radiographic texture trajectories, particularly for Contrast and SRE. These findings indicate quantitative imaging differences rather than direct evidence of impaired osseointegration and warrant prospective validation.

papers.abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to investigate the corrosion resistance of three types of Co–Cr alloys manufactured by casting or selective laser melting (SLM). Six Co–Cr dental alloys were classified into three different types according to their formulation (containing Mo, W, or both as alloying elements) and according to the manufacturing process, namely, casting or SLM. Then the electrochemical properties were characterized by Anodic Polarization Scanning (AS) and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) in Ringer's and 0.1 M NaCl +0.1 M lactic acid solutions. E corr , I corr , E pit , and corrosion rate (CR) were estimated by AS and statistically analyzed ( α = 0.05). The EIS data fitted to a Randles circuit. Electrochemical testing revealed statistically significant differences for E corr and E pit among the alloys tested in the same solution, whereas no differences were identified in I corr or CR. The Nyquist plots exhibited semicircular profiles, indicating that the electrochemical response was predominantly controlled by charge transfer processes. For all groups, CR was found much higher in the acidic 0.1 M lactic acid + 0.1 M NaCl solution than in Ringer's one. The results of this study showed that CR depended on the solution rather than alloy type or manufacturing process.

The framework is validated against experimental compression tests on additively manufactured thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) specimens, with errors below 3%. The resulting dataset underpins forward and inverse deep neural network (DNN) models for energy absorption prediction and optimal thickness-distribution identification. A physics-guided neural network (PGNN) is further developed by embedding a regression-derived thickness-energy relationship as a hard constraint in the loss function. PGNN achieves reliable extrapolation beyond the training domain with errors below 2.5%, and reaches stable convergence with only 10 training samples compared with 2145 required by the conventional DNN. The proposed framework establishes a computationally efficient and physically consistent approach for the inverse design of thickness-graded auxetic metamaterials, demonstrated here for the investigated enhanced re-entrant architecture and with potential for extension to other graded lattice configurations.

papers.title: Understanding Spatter and Its Spatial Variations in Laser Powder Bed Fusion of Ti6Al4V
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) by laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) is rapidly developing as a principal method for the manufacture of metal parts. However, widespread adoption of the technology, especially for safety-critical applications, is impeded by complications to achieving the desired component quality and reliability. Spatter occurs due to interactions between the laser and the melt pool and involves the ejection of material from within or about its vicinity. Recognized as a process signature in L-PBF, spatter is considered detrimental to build quality. However, relationships between spatter kinetics and part defects have remained largely underexplored. In this investigation, spatter is evaluated via in situ optical tomography (OT) imaging acquired during builds performed with Ti6Al4V powder. Results showed that the volume of spatter content is greater at particular scan angles as well as specific locations in the build chamber. Furthermore, the spatter dynamics behave differently upwind and downwind of printed regions and indicate that local variations in gas flow can be inferred from spatter signatures. As spatter is known to directly cause defects in parts produced by L-PBF, regions with increased spatter potentially signal reduced metal quality. Variations in the spatter content are identified and regions of the build at greater risk for defects are highlighted.

papers.title: Discrete time phased Petri box calculus dtphPBC
papers.abstract: We propose discrete time phased Petri box calculus (dtphPBC), an extension with phase type delays of discrete time stochastic and deterministic Petri box calculus (dtsdPBC). In dtphPBC, transition probability matrices (TPMs) of finite absorbing discrete time Markov chains with a single absorbing state specify discrete phase type (DPH) delays (including zero delay) of the phased multiactions that generalize stochastic and deterministic ones from dtsdPBC. The positively phased (timed) multiactions have positive DPH delays represented by the non-empty TPM matrices over transient states (transient TPMs). The zero phased (immediate) multiactions have zero DPH delay represented by the empty transient TPM. The step operational semantics of dtphPBC is constructed via labeled probabilistic transition systems.

papers.abstract: Abstract Decked-charge blasting includes axially discontinuous or decoupled charge configurations, with air-deck blasting as one subtype. Here, air-deck denotes an intentional air or gaseous void, whereas decked-charge includes air, water, expanded-polystyrene (EPS), and polyethylene (PE) decks. Published fragmentation results remain inconsistent because rock conditions, blast geometry, deck design, response definition, and reporting differ across studies. This study develops a literature-derived, source-aware evidence-synthesis and exploratory interpretable-modelling framework. A dataset of 42 observations and 114 fields from six sources was reconstructed; 30 observations from four sources were regression-eligible, comprising 20 air-deck, two water-deck, one EPS-deck, one PE-deck, and six conventional/no-deck cases. Random Forest achieved leave-one-out MAE = 82.29 mm, RMSE = 126.50 mm, and R 2 = 0.391. Bayesian optimization improved tuning-stage performance, but nested leave-one-source-out validation remained weak. Independent external validation on 31 field cases from three unseen publications yielded a best pooled result of MAE = 134.64 mm, RMSE = 158.27 mm, and R 2 = − 0.194; all evaluated models had negative external R 2 . Explainability identified response family, rock strength, burden-to-diameter ratio, hole depth, observation scale, hole diameter, specific charge, stemming, bench-height-to-burden ratio, and deck position as influential. Sensitivity analysis showed that within-dataset associations were not driven solely by response family, while cross-source transfer remained limited by source and response-definition heterogeneity. Source-level comparison found smaller fragmentation in 11 of 18 paired cases (mean − 21.91%; median − 31.48%). Air-decking should therefore be treated as a site- and configuration-dependent option requiring local verification, and the framework as an evidence-synthesis tool rather than a direct blast-design predictor.

papers.title: Machine Learning and Explainable AI for Slope Stability Assessment: A Systematic Review of Methods, Parameters, and Research Gaps
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used to predict the factor of safety (FoS) and stability state of slopes, often combined with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). This PRISMA 2020 systematic review searched OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Crossref (2000–2026), screened 6,550 unique records, mapped 1,009 eligible studies at abstract level and synthesised 137 open-access full texts. Publications grew sharply after 2020, and artificial neural networks are giving way to tree ensembles, deep learning and metaheuristic hybrids. Reported performance is high (median test 2 0.97; median accuracy 0.93) but rests mainly on synthetic limit-equilibrium or finite-element data (51 % of studies) or on small, overlapping compilations of published case histories (median 190 cases). Only 11 % of studies addressed data quality or duplicates, 39 % used cross-validation, 4 % validated on independent cases and 15 % shared code or data. Class thresholds ranged from FoS 1.0 to 1.3. About half of the studies reported explanations, mostly feature importance, sensitivity analysis or SHAP, but none validated them quantitatively against limit-equilibrium sensitivities. Priorities are curated public datasets, leakage-aware and external validation, explicit target definitions, uncertainty quantification and mechanics-based validation of explanations. Key Words: slope stability, factor of safety, machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, systematic review, PRISMA

papers.abstract: This study develops an interpretable point-and-interval prediction method for mine ventilation-parameter identification using limited field samples. Guided by ventilation-resistance theory, eight engineering attributes—roadway length, width, height, cross-sectional area, wetted perimeter, equivalent diameter, support type, and cross-sectional shape—were selected, and a prediction dataset was constructed from 260 field samples. The extended Random Feature Model (xRFM) establishes a nonlinear mapping, and the proposed Evolution-Path Guided Ivy Algorithm (EPG-IVY) optimizes hyperparameters within the training data. Prediction intervals are then constructed from out-of-fold residuals using Adaptive Bandwidth Kernel Density Estimation (ABKDE), while SHAP is used to analyze the model’s dependence on engineering features. With a fixed 7:3 split, EPG-IVY-xRFM achieved R2 = 0.9754, RMSE = 0.001600, and MAE = 0.001162. Repeated nested five-fold cross-validation yielded R2 = 0.9719 ± 0.0084, RMSE = 0.001675 ± 0.000267, and MAE = 0.001225 ± 0.000182, with lower RMSE and MAE than the optimized XGBoost and CatBoost baselines. External validation on 28 independent samples from Balasu Coal Mine yielded R2 = 0.890, RMSE = 0.007072, and MAE = 0.003873. The empirical coverage of the 90% ABKDE prediction interval was 0.8846, and its Wilson 95% confidence interval included the nominal coverage level. SHAP results identified support type, roadway width, and equivalent diameter as the main contributing factors in the current model. These results provide a data-driven framework for friction resistance coefficient identification with point prediction, uncertainty estimation, and feature attribution under limited field samples.

papers.title: Rapid residual stress assessment in additively manufactured specimens via standard uniaxial tensile testing
papers.abstract: Abstract High residual stresses (RS) in laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) components present significant structural challenges, yet traditional characterization techniques are cost- and time-intensive. This study introduces three rapid mechanical testing methodologies to estimate longitudinal RS in PBF-LB 316 L stainless steel by using the premature micro-yielding of pre-tensioned near-surface regions in cylindrical geometries. The proposed methods evaluate RS through: (I) plastic work density calculated from cyclic loading-unloading, (II) virtual unloading mathematically projected from standard monotonic tensile data, which also allows the analysis of existing tensile test results, and (III) the detection of a macroscopic micro-yielding threshold (0.01% strain). The estimates were benchmarked against neutron diffraction (ND) measurements across multiple heat-treatment conditions (as-built to 1000 °C). The energy-based approaches (Proposed Methods I and II) demonstrated linear correlations with relative ND stress reductions (R 2 = 0.75 and 0.71, respectively). Furthermore, by subtracting the empirical micro-yielding threshold from condition-specific macroscopic yield strengths, Proposed Method III captured the relative RS relaxation trend. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis supported the proposed mechanistic interpretation by showing localized geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) accumulation prior to bulk yielding. These findings show that the proposed mechanical methods can serve as accessible tools for evaluating stress mitigation strategies in additive manufacturing.

papers.title: A Caputo fractional physics-informed neural network for Lorenz chaotic systems
papers.abstract: Fractional-order dynamical systems provide an effective mathematical framework for describing nonlinear processes with memory and hereditary effects. Although physics-informed neural networks have demonstrated promising performance for solving differential equations, their application to fractional-order chaotic dynamical systems remains relatively limited. In this study, a Caputo fractional physics-informed neural networks (FPINNs) framework is developed to approximate the fractional-order Lorenz system by incorporating the governing fractional differential equations into a multi-objective loss function. The reference solutions are generated using the Caputo Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM) predictor-corrector method to ensure an appropriate numerical treatment of the fractional derivative. The proposed framework is evaluated for several fractional orders over the considered simulation interval, and its predictive performance is assessed using quantitative error metrics, including mean squared error, mean absolute error, sum of squared errors, and the coefficient of determination. The numerical results demonstrate that the FPINN accurately reconstructs the fractional Lorenz trajectories while maintaining good agreement with the ABM reference solutions. Furthermore, the study investigates the influence of the fractional order on prediction accuracy and computational performance, providing a systematic numerical assessment of the proposed framework. The results indicate that FPINNs constitute an effective and data-efficient approach for approximating nonlinear fractional dynamical systems within the investigated computational setting.

papers.title: Isothermal annealing optimization for enhanced mechanical performance of FFF-printed PEKK gyroid structures
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to establish a systematic isothermal annealing post-treatment to mitigate residual stress and poor interlayer adhesion inherent in fused filament fabrication (FFF) of polyetherketoneketone (PEKK), thereby enhancing the mechanical performance of printed components. The optimized protocol is further extended to gyroid triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures to evaluate its broader applicability. Design/methodology/approach Thermal transitions and stability were characterized via differential scanning calorimetry and thermogravimetric analysis, revealing a glass transition temperature of ∼218 °C and stability up to 542 °C. X-ray diffraction and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed predominantly amorphous behavior. Annealing was conducted at 180, 200, 220, 240 and 260 °C for 6 h under constrained conditions followed by furnace cooling, with flexural testing used for the optimization. Failure mechanisms were examined via digital microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. The optimized protocol was validated on cylindrical gyroid structures under compression. Findings Annealing at 240°C increased flexural modulus and strength by 58.7 % and 72.7 %, respectively, shifting failure from delamination to bulk fracture. For gyroid structures, compressive modulus and yield strength improved by 16.7% and 23.2%. Enhancements stemmed from stress relaxation and improved interlayer bonding rather than crystallinity changes. Originality/value This work combines thermal analysis, molecular simulation and failure characterization to explain why annealing improves the performance of amorphous FFF-printed PEKK and provides a practical route for post-processing optimization of complex PEKK structures.

papers.title: Functionally Graded Metal Metamaterials: Additive Manufacturing, Materials, Architectures, Intelligent Design and Industrial Application—A Review
papers.abstract: Functionally Graded Metamaterials (FGMMs) refer to new categories of materials whose design through variation in composition and geometry leads to the attainment of properties that cannot be realized using regular materials. The use of additive manufacturing (AM) offers the necessary flexibility in terms of geometry for creating such designs. This research topic was selected due to an increase in the use of metamaterials and architectural gradients in AM, along with the need to establish the relationship between gradients in design, process, structure, and performance. In this review, a comprehensive study will be conducted regarding metallic FGMMs fabricated using additive manufacturing. The methods to be studied include gradient design, lattice and Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) geometries, Directed Energy Deposition (DED), Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM), Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF), Electron Beam Melting (EBM), the future of AM, composition gradient in metals, topology optimization, multiscale design, and machine learning. The literature review indicates that material and architectural gradients can produce features such as controlled deformation, lightweighting, energy dissipation, heat dissipation, and multifunctional design. DED and WAAM provide the freedom of grading composition and large-scale manufacturing, whereas LPBF has a higher resolution for lattice and TPMS geometries. Topology optimization and machine learning are helping with designing the materials and architecture with regard to performance, but there are still some constraints due to data dependency, generalizability, manufacturability, and physical constraints. Some of the challenges facing implementation include defects, residual stresses, cracking, intermetallic formation, process variability, and post-processing. Even sustainability depends on the material choice, energy usage, processing, manufacturing volume, and lifecycle. In general, the review points out that there is a need for a design-to-manufacturing approach that brings together materials selection, structural design, process control, and smart design techniques for the development of metallic FGMMs.

papers.title: Fault diagnosis and uncertainty quantification for the shaft system of hydropower units based on center-frequency positional encoding and variational Bayesian transformer
papers.abstract: Abstract Fault samples of hydropower unit shaft systems can hardly cover all conditions, so unknown states outside the training distribution inevitably appear in online monitoring data. Most existing deep diagnostic models are deterministic: they output a single class label, and can neither characterize the credibility of their own conclusions nor exploit the physical prior of the frequency bands occupied by the modal components. This paper therefore proposes MSEF-BayesFormer, a probabilistic diagnosis model integrating multi-scale entropy features into a variational Bayesian Transformer. A multi-scale entropy feature convolutional embedding module is proposed, in which the refined composite multiscale permutation entropy matrix of the modal components obtained by variational mode decomposition, instead of raw-waveform patches, serves as the input and is mapped into a token sequence by depthwise separable convolution, suppressing at the source the interference of noise on the representation and making fault patterns well separable before they enter the attention interaction. A center-frequency positional encoding is proposed, in which the normalized center frequency of each intrinsic mode function modulates the angular frequency of the sinusoidal positional encoding of the Transformer, explicitly injecting frequency-band physical mechanism information into the model. The attention weights are extended from point estimates to variational Gaussian distributions and trained end-to-end via the evidence lower bound; Monte Carlo sampling yields the predictive distribution, and the predictive uncertainty is decomposed into aleatoric and epistemic components. On a rotor test rig with four condition classes, the average five-fold cross-validation accuracy reaches 0.9523, 2.48 percentage points higher than the deterministic Transformer; the area under the risk–coverage curve is 0.40, better than 0.64 of Deep Ensemble; and the average AUROC of leave-one-class-out unknown-state detection is 0.8139, exceeding MC Dropout and Deep Ensemble by 0.13 and 0.18. In the hydraulic unbalance case at the SK hydropower station, the dominant frequency band on which the model relies is locked onto the blade passing frequency, consistent with the excitation mechanism of this fault.

papers.title: Document world models: a cognitive-inspired auxiliary training framework for document-level relation extraction
papers.abstract: Document-level Relation Extraction (DocRE) requires models to integrate relation evidence scattered across multiple sentences. Yet existing encoder-based methods perform relation classification in a single pass over a static final representation, causing long-range evidence to decay before it can inform the classification decision. Inspired by theories of incremental reading comprehension, we introduce the Document World Model (DocWM), a lightweight training-only auxiliary framework that encourages progressive entity-state maintenance and relation-belief stabilization in standard DocRE encoders. DocWM introduces two auxiliary training objectives. Entity State Tracking (ES) maintains an entity-specific recurrent hidden state, updated sentence by sentence and aligned with entity embeddings pooled from mentions up to each sentence to preserve early evidence. Relation Belief Dynamics (BD) supervises relation predictions at each reading step via a temporally weighted loss, guiding relation beliefs to stabilize progressively toward the correct label. Experiments on Re-DocRED and HacRED show consistent improvements over the compared baselines, most clearly on long-range cross-sentence relations.

papers.title: Leadership Development Programmes for Clinical Nurses: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To provide a comprehensive understanding of the current leadership development programmes for clinical nurses. Design Systematic review was designed and reported in accordance with the PRISMA and Synthesis Without Meta‐analysis (SWiM) guidelines. Data Sources Four electronic databases from 2014 to 2026 studies published were searched. Methods A comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed, Cochrane, Scopus and Web of Science. English, full‐text literature from 2014 to 2026. This systematic review was registered with PROSPERO under the number CRD42024587447. Results A systematic review of 18 studies showed that leadership development programmes significantly improved nurses' relational leadership skills (transformational, paternalistic, authentic, resonant and caring), job satisfaction, organizational commitment and self‐efficacy, while reducing emotional exhaustion. For nurse managers, these programmes enhance care management knowledge, build healthier work environments and strengthen the hospital safety climates. Incorporating active learning methods, such as simulations, role‐playing, reflective practice and 360° feedback, improves engagement and skill retention. Conclusion Studies show that the conceptual framework of leadership programmes for nurses and nurse managers varies with the skills/behaviours they aim to develop, and there is no standardization regarding the programme duration. However, evidence on their impact on institutional and patient outcomes remains limited. These gaps and variables should be considered when structuring leadership programmes in future research. Relevance to Clinical Practice Relevant for clinical nurses, nurse managers and healthcare organizations, with potential to enhance retention, professional growth and indirectly patient care quality. There is a lack of standardized leadership development programmes and insufficient evidence on their impact on organizational and patient outcomes. Programmes improved nurses' leadership competencies, commitment, satisfaction and self‐efficacy, while reducing exhaustion; nurse managers gained caring and authentic leadership skills. papers.title: Uncertainty quantification in SST k-ω and standard k-ϵ turbulence models for aerodynamic simulations of high-Speed trains under crosswind conditions
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of the aerodynamic loads on high-speed trains (HSTs) under crosswind conditions is essential for reliable safety assessment. However, the empirical closure coefficients embedded in Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) turbulence models introduce parametric uncertainty that may propagate substantially into aerodynamic predictions. This study presents a controlled comparative analysis of closure-coefficient uncertainty in the Standard k-ϵ and Shear Stress Transport (SST) k-ω models under an identical numerical framework. Latin hypercube sampling and non-intrusive polynomial chaos are employed for uncertainty propagation, together with total-order Sobol indices and correlation analysis to characterise global and spatial parameter sensitivities. The results show that the lateral force coefficient (Cy) is particularly sensitive to closure-coefficient variations, with UQ2 values of 43.95% for the Standard k-ϵ model and 50.78% for the SST k-ω model. Although the SST k-ω model exhibits more localised pressure uncertainty in several separated-flow regions, it does not consistently yield lower uncertainty in the integrated aerodynamic loads. The two models also display fundamentally different sensitivity patterns. The Standard k-ϵ model is strongly dominated by Cε2, which contributes a total-order Sobol index of 0.9835 to Cy, whereas the SST k-ω model exhibits distributed multi-parameter sensitivity, with σω1 providing the largest contribution of 0.5100. These parameters are also strongly correlated with Cy, with Pearson correlation coefficients of −0.7768 and −0.7089, respectively. The results demonstrate that turbulence-model calibration for HST crosswind aerodynamics should account for model-dependent parameter sensitivity and provide a quantitative basis for uncertainty-aware model selection and calibration.

papers.abstract: Adolescent depression has one of the major public health concerns due to its negative impacts on psychological well-being, academic success, and social functioning. Proactive detection of adolescent at risk is essential for timely support and assistance; however, conventional statistical methods may not adequately capture the complex nonlinear relationships among behavioral, lifestyle and psychological factors. The present study investigated the performance of five supervised machine learning approaches for predicting adolescent depression utilizing a publicly available Teen Mental Health Dataset. To improve model performance, class imbalance was addressed using Adaptive Synthetic Sampling and Bayesian optimization was applied for hyperparameter tuning. Model performance was assessed using different metrices and was further examined through learning curve analysis, repeated stratified cross validation and non-parametric statistical tests. Among evaluated models XGBoost and CatBoost achieved the best predictive performance, outperforming the remaining classifiers across all evaluation metrics. Friedman and Wilcoxon signed rank test confirmed significant differences in model performance. Model interpretation using SHAP and LIME consistently identified sleep duration, stress level, anxiety level, and daily social media use as the most important factors associated with adolescent depression. These results shows that predictive machine learning models can help to the early identification of adolescents at risk of depression while providing valuable insights into the behavioral factors associated with mental health. Such information may assist clinicians, educators and public health practitioners in developing targeted screening and early intervention strategies.

papers.title: Multiple source-free domain adaptation via efficient-DDPM and adaptive fine-grained weight integration for imbalanced fault diagnosis
papers.abstract: Reliable operation of rotating machinery is pivotal to industrial production safety and efficiency. Constrained by data privacy concerns, source-free domain adaptation has emerged as a research focus in fault diagnosis, as it avoids the need to access source domain data. However, target domain data collected from real-world industrial scenarios often suffer from class imbalance and distribution shift, which severely degrade diagnostic performance. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel multiple source-free domain adaptation method based on efficient denoising diffusion probabilistic model (Efficient-DDPM) and adaptive fine-grained weight integration for imbalanced fault diagnosis. Specifically, the Efficient-DDPM utilizes extremely few labeled target-domain fault samples to generate high-quality synthetic samples for minority fault classes. It incorporates an improved U-Net architecture and optimized time steps to enhance both sample quality and computational efficiency. Meanwhile, multiple pretrained source models are introduced to provide richer prior knowledge, and a dual-attention enhancement module is developed to learn intra-domain and inter-domain integration weights, achieving an optimal balance between sample specificity and domain consistency. In addition, a loss reweighting strategy guided by uncertainty quantification is constructed to mitigate the impact of low-quality pseudo-labels. Experiments on two bearing datasets verify that the proposed method achieves superior cross-domain diagnostic performance under constraints of data privacy and class imbalance, confirming its effectiveness and practicality.

papers.title: Conceptual Integration and Research Trends in Radioisotope Production Simulation Using PHITS: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: Accelerator-based radioisotope production, particularly within cyclotron target systems, plays a critical role in modern nuclear medicine for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. The complexity of particle interactions, target geometry, and the formation of primary and secondary radionuclides limits purely experimental approaches. Consequently, Monte Carlo–based simulation using the Particle and Heavy Ion Transport code System (PHITS) has emerged as a strategic tool for comprehensive radionuclide production and radioactivity assessment of cyclotron target systems. This study employed a systematic literature review integrated with bibliometric analysis to examine PHITS-based radioisotope production research. Article selection followed the PRISMA framework using the Scopus database (2004–2025). Seven research articles explicitly applying PHITS-based Monte Carlo simulations were retained. Findings indicate increasing publication activity after 2018, dominated by countries with advanced nuclear infrastructure, particularly Japan. Theoretical synthesis identified four principal domains: target design optimization, Monte Carlo code validation, specific isotope production, and infrastructure development. The framework further revealed research gaps including integrated multi-parameter modeling, uncertainty quantification, time-dependent simulation, and techno-economic assessment. PHITS-based Monte Carlo simulation represents a robust framework for analyzing cyclotron target radioactivity and supports the transition toward integrative, predictive, and application-oriented radioisotope production research.

papers.title: Microstructure, crystallographic texture, and enhanced wear and hardness properties of 2 wt.% Nb-modified 316L stainless steel fabricated by wire arc additive manufacturing at different deposition orientations
papers.abstract: Abstract Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) has become a highly dependable manufacturing technique in the 21st century due to its cost-effectiveness, shortened production time, and reduced material wastage. Compared with other additive manufacturing techniques such as selective laser melting and electron beam electron beam melting, WAAM offers significantly higher deposition rates, lower feedstock costs, and greater capability for producing large-scale metallic components. Due to these advantages, WAAM has gained considerable attention in industries requiring large structural components and complex geometries. WAAM excels particularly in fabricating complex geometries. However, defects remain a significant challenge associated with WAAM-deposited stainless steel. The objective of this study is to investigate the influence of (Nb) addition on the microstructural characteristics, mechanical properties and mechanical behavior of WAAM deposited 316 L fabricated under different build orientations and interlayer time. WAAM deposited cubes 316L stainless steel were fabricated at the three deposition orientations (0°,67°, and 90°) with interlayer times of 2 and 5 min. The addition of 2% Nb was intended to modify the microstructure and enhance the mechanical and tribological properties of the deposited material. Details microstructural characterization were performed using electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), and X-ray diffraction (XRD). These techniques were used to analyze grain morphology, phase distribution, crystallographic orientations, and microstructural variations along the build direction. Mechanical and tribological properties were evaluated through hardness measurements and dry sliding wear tests. wear experiments were conducted using pin-on-disk tribometer to investigate the coefficient of friction (COF) and wear behavior of the WAAM—deposited material. The results indicate that build orientation significantly influences the tribological performance of the deposited material. For the 0° orientation, the coefficient of friction ranges from 0.57 to 0.64, whereas the 67° orientation shows a slightly lower COF ranging from 0.55 to 0.58. The addition of 2% Nb contributes to improved microstructural stability and enhanced wear performance. The novelty of this research lies in the incorporation of Nb into WAAM- fabricated 316L stainless steel to improve microstructural characteristics, mechanical and tribological properties.

papers.title: Metaverse-based active learning in higher education: evidence from a large-scale educational innovation project
papers.abstract: Background The incorporation of the metaverse into the university setting is generating growing interest due to its potential to transform educational processes through immersive experiences and active methodologies. However, existing studies tend to focus on pilot programs or technology acceptance, with few analyzing large-scale institutional implementation and its contribution to the digital transformation of universities. Objective To evaluate the institutional implementation of an immersive learning ecosystem based on active methodologies and the metaverse, analyzing its scalability, academic reach, and organizational components to foster educational innovation and digital competence within a university institution. Method A descriptive study of institutional evaluation based on consolidated records of an educational innovation project carried out in one private university in Peru during the year 2025. Data were obtained from institutional dashboards and project monitoring databases, including indicators related to students, teachers, academic programs, subjects, technological resources, and implementation phases. The study included a descriptive statistical analysis and an integrated evaluation of institutional indicators. Results The project reached 994 students across four implementation phases, following a progressive scaling process with broad participation from degree programs, courses, and faculty. This implementation established an institutional ecosystem underpinned by the integration of active methodologies, metaverse-based immersive environments, digital educational resources, and management strategies aimed at ensuring the innovation’s sustainability. Four key characteristics of the institutional model were identified: scalability, interdisciplinary reach, pedagogical integration, and organizational capacity. Conclusions The institutional implementation of the immersive learning ecosystem represents an educational transformation that goes beyond mere technological adoption. It demonstrates the potential to integrate digital infrastructure, active methodologies, faculty training, and institutional management into a scalable model of educational innovation. The study provides evidence for universities interested in developing immersive ecosystems to strengthen digital competence and consolidate sustainable digital transformation processes.

papers.title: SOLVING NONLINEAR BOUNDARY VALUE PROBLEMS FOR ORDINARY DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS USING PHYSICS-INFORMED NEURAL NETWORKS: ANALYSIS OF COLLOCATION POINT SELECTION STRATEGIES
papers.abstract: The use of differential equations remains relevant for studying processes in various applied fields, where they have proven to be an effective tool for describing the motion of mechanical and oscillatory systems, modeling electrical circuits, heat and mass transfer processes, chemical kinetics, and biologicalphenomena such as the spread of diseases and population dynamics. The solution of boundary value problems based on the corresponding equations makes it possible to determine the state of an object over time or at different points in space, as well as to analyze its stability under changes in model parameters or external conditions. The complexity and adequacy of a mathematical model depend on the type of differential equation used. To account for complex patterns, nonlinear differential equations or their systems are typically employed. However, despite their widespread use in applied research, exact analytical solutions for such equations have been obtained only in particular cases, while in most situations they are difficult or impossible to derive. Under these conditions, numerical solution methods are applied, allowing one to obtain approximate solutions of boundary value problems on a set of points (a grid) with a prescribed accuracy. The effective use of numerical methods is associated with computational tools that combine high accuracy with acceptable computational cost. At the same time, the development of computer technologies has enabled not only the automation of classical numerical algorithms but also the emergence of new approaches, in particular those based on neural networks (Physics-Informed Neural Networks, PINNs). One of the key issues in the use of PINNs is the assessment of the accuracy of the obtained solutions. In this work, the quality of solutions obtained by PINNs for certain nonlinear second-order differential equations with boundary conditions (using the classical Bratu problem as an example) is investigated by comparing them with analytical (exact) and numerical solutions. Conclusions are drawn based on a comparison of uniform and adaptive selection strategies for PINN collocation points.

papers.abstract: Gas turbines are widely used in modern power generation due to their high efficiency and flexibility. However, using exhaust silencers in exhaust gas systems can increase back pressure, reducing overall turbine performance. The aerodynamic behavior of the splitter inside the exhaust silencer, especially at the trailing edge, significantly affects pressure drop and turbulence intensity. This study aims to optimize the trailing edge geometry of a GE Frame 6FA exhaust silencer splitter using a combination of computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and Bayesian optimization (BO). CFD simulations were conducted in ANSYS Fluent using a poly-hexcore mesh, while the optimization employed a Gaussian process (GP) surrogate model with an expected improvement (EI) acquisition function. Seven trailing edge angles (5°–20°) were evaluated to observe the aerodynamic trade-off between pressure drop and turbulent kinetic energy (TKE). The optimal configuration was found at 13.9°, yielding a TKE of 0.43 J/kg and a pressure drop of 18.38 Pa, well below the industrial allowable pressure drop limit of 34 Pa. The results confirm that the BO-GP framework effectively reduces computational cost while achieving a more aerodynamically balanced silencer design.

papers.title: Robust multi-criteria decision-making of additive manufacturing processes under preference variability: a Monte-Carlo and graph-based framework
papers.abstract: Abstract Metal Additive Manufacturing (AM) process selection is affected by uncertainty in techno-economic data and decision makers’ preferences. When competing technologies achieve similar overall performances, deterministic Multi-Criteria Decision-Making methods may produce strict rankings that do not adequately reflect the robustness of the underlying evidence. This work proposes a methodological framework for interpreting probabilistic Analytic Hierarchy Process results obtained through Monte Carlo simulation. Pairwise comparisons are modelled as random variables, generating distributions of global scores for the evaluated alternatives. Rather than relying only on mean scores or rank acceptability measures, the proposed framework analyses pairwise outscoring probabilities derived from the simulated scores. These probabilities are jointly represented through a dendrogram and a graph structure, allowing the identification of robust dominance relationships and equivalence classes among alternatives. The methodology is illustrated through a literature-based case study comparing Bound Metal Deposition and single- and multi-laser Laser Powder Bed Fusion systems under different industrial production scenarios. The results show that the proposed post-analysis framework reveals which ranking distinctions remain supported under uncertainty and which alternatives cannot be reliably distinguished. In particular, high-production scenarios reveal weak preferential separation between BMD and multi-laser L-PBF, suggesting that both technologies should be regarded as equivalent candidates rather than forcing a strict ranking. The proposed framework is particularly suited to support decisions involving emerging additive manufacturing technologies, where limited industrial maturity and uncertain techno-economic information often make strict deterministic rankings difficult to justify.

papers.title: Machine learning for biomarker-driven thalassemia diagnosis: a framework for causal effect estimation
papers.abstract: Thalassemia is one of the most heterogeneous diseases, with more than a thousand mutation types recorded worldwide. Molecular diagnosis of thalassemia by conventional PCR-based DNA analysis is time- and resource-consuming owing to the phenotype variability, disease complexity, and molecular diagnostic test limitations. Thalassemia diagnosis relies heavily on complex interactions among hematological biomarkers, making it challenging to distinguish causal relationships from mere statistical correlations. To address this limitation, this study proposes a causal machine learning framework that integrates causal discovery and counterfactual inference to identify biomarker-driven treatment effects for thalassemia diagnosis. The proposed approach models clinical variables using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to capture underlying causal dependencies and enables robust estimation of treatment effects while accounting for confounding factors. To address the primary objective from complementary causal perspectives, the framework combines adjusted regression for confounding control, inverse probability weighting for propensity-based estimation, Random Forest-based analysis for nonlinear feature importance and heterogeneous treatment effects, and bootstrap resampling for uncertainty quantification. The adjusted linear regression model yielded a conservative causal effect estimate of 0.3008, while propensity-based methods demonstrated stronger effects, with IPW producing an estimate of 1.0604. The bootstrap approach confirmed the stability of these findings with a 95% confidence interval of [0.8806, 1.2161], indicating statistically significant treatment influence. Furthermore, heterogeneous effect analysis using CATE revealed substantial variability across individuals, with estimates ranging between 0.0848 and 2.5200, highlighting the importance of personalized assessment. Stratified analysis across age groups showed distinct differences, with the highest effect observed in adolescents (1.3484) and lower effects in children (0.8856), emphasizing demographic-specific variations. The results demonstrate that key biomarkers, particularly hemoglobin-related features, exert significant causal influence on thalassemia diagnosis.

papers.abstract: Objective: This review critically examined artificial intelligence (AI) applications in canine echocardiography, automated measurement and disease classification strategies, validation designs, and the requirements for safe clinical translation. Method: A narrative review was conducted. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched on 20 October 2026, supplemented by screening the reference lists of identified articles, and studies that applied machine learning or deep learning to canine echocardiograms were selected by relevance. Results: In the clinical veterinary setting, two studies addressed automated ventricular measurements through anatomical landmark localization and staging of myxomatous mitral valve disease through echocardiography–radiography fusion. An additional group of experimental studies applied deep learning to left ventricular segmentation and motion tracking in dogs. The main challenges identified were operator variability, breed-related anatomical heterogeneity, the lack of multicenter validation, and reliance on imperfect reference standards. Conclusions: The clinical usefulness of these models requires patient- and center-level evaluation, uncertainty quantification, agreement studies against specialists, and analysis of errors near treatment thresholds. A two-stage research pathway, measurement followed by classification, was proposed, complemented by prospective assessment and veterinary oversight.

papers.title: Infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TiO2 nanotube surfaces: mechanisms and synergistic design strategies
papers.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanotubes (TNTs) fabricated via anodization have emerged as a versatile platform for surface modification of orthopedic and dental implants, owing to their tunable nanotopography and excellent potential for multifunctional biofunctionalization. However, the concurrent challenges of implant-associated bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration remain formidable obstacles in clinical practice. Rather than being independent processes, bacterial infection and bone regeneration are intimately coupled through a complex signaling network—a concept increasingly recognized as the “infection-osteogenesis crosstalk.” We begin with how TNT morphology—nanotube diameter above all—differentially steers osteoblast behavior and bacterial adhesion, and how the initial protein corona and immune microenvironment set the infection-to-bone-healing trajectory. From signaling, we move to the pathways behind infection-driven osteogenic suppression: the core signaling pathways through which bacterial virulence factors suppress osteogenesis, including TLR-mediated NF-κB activation, RANKL/OPG imbalance-driven osteoclastogenesis, and biofilm hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming. We then look at how macrophages (M1/M2 polarization, NLRP3 inflammasome), neutrophils (NETosis), and T cells shape the host response to infection and bone repair. We close with current synergistic design strategies—metal ion doping, antimicrobial peptide loading, organic-inorganic composite coatings, temporally controlled drug release—and next-generation smart responsive surfaces including pH-responsive, photothermal/photocatalytic, enzyme-responsive, and immunomodulatory coatings. This review aims to provide a mechanistic framework for understanding infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TNT surfaces and to guide the rational design of dual-functional implants that simultaneously combat infection and promote bone regeneration.

papers.title: Improving stochastic dynamic programming for reservoir operation using drought severity and the copula function
papers.abstract: Study region Marun Dam reservoir, southwestern Iran. Study focus Reservoir operation under droughts remains challenging because traditional Stochastic Dynamic Programming (SDP) estimates inflow transition probabilities using Markov chains, without explicitly considering drought severity or nonlinear dependence between hydrological variables. This study reformulates the transition probability matrix (TPM) of SDP by integrating inflow and drought severity into the TPM using copula functions, specifying more realistic reservoir operation policies under drought conditions. To achieve this, the Copula-Hybrid Drought Index (CHDI) is proposed, based on the predicted rainfall projections acquired from the results of modeled climate-change simulations under the SSP3.70 scenario. New hydrological insights for the region Historical analysis of Marun Dam reservoir shows that the implementation of the proposed SDP, integrating inflow with the drought severity for the previous period using copula-based transition probabilities (TPM C ), yields greater sustainability and conserves more water in the reservoir for future ‎droughts‎, compared with the SDP method using the conventional Markov-chain transition probabilities (TPM M ). However, this improvement comes with a higher objective ‎function value. The proposed approach is also examined using three suggested scenarios, named S1, S2, and S3, to update the operation policies under droughts, and shows a reduction in drought severity and duration of drought spells by reserving more water for the drought periods, albeit at the cost of lower sustainability and objective function values. This research confirms that incorporating inflow with drought through TPMs enhances the robustness of reservoir operation policies under drought conditions, particularly for arid and semi-arid regions facing increasing climate variability.

papers.title: Bone anabolic agents repair alveolar bone damaged by diabetes in mice.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a chronic metabolic disorder that significantly impacts skeletal health, including bones of the oral cavity, where alveolar bone is particularly susceptible due to its high remodeling rate and sensitivity to systemic metabolic changes. Using a mouse model of established T2D induced by high-fat diet and streptozotocin, we investigated the effects of the FDA-approved bone anabolic agents parathyroid hormone (PTH) and abaloparatide (ABL) on alveolar bone. In non-diabetic mice, PTH and ABL stimulated both bone formation and resorption, resulting in no net change in alveolar bone mass. In contrast, these agents selectively increased bone formation in T2D mice without further enhancing the already elevated resorption, leading to net alveolar bone gain. This anabolic effect involves suppression of sclerostin and Dickkopf-1 (Dkk-1) in osteocytes and activation of Wnt signaling in periodontal ligament cells. Studies using DMP1-Cre;PTH1Rfl/fl mice demonstrated that osteocytic PTH1R is essential for the anabolic effects but not for the bone resorption-promoting effects of PTH and ABL. These findings reveal a dual mechanism of PTH1R signaling in oral bone remodeling and suggest therapeutic strategies to restore alveolar bone and improve tooth retention and implant osseointegration in diabetic patients.

papers.title: Advanced cannabidiol delivery platforms: smart biomaterials, controlled release systems, and 3D-bioprinted therapeutic technologies.
papers.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid derived from Cannabis sativa L. has gained significant attention in biomedical research due to its broad spectrum of therapeutic properties, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antioxidant, neuroprotective, and anticancer activities. However, its clinical translation remains limited by poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, rapid metabolism, and instability under physiological conditions. To overcome these challenges, advanced drug delivery platforms based on 3D bioprinting technologies have emerged as promising strategies for controlled and site-specific delivery of CBD. This review provides a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art CBD delivery systems, including polymeric biomaterials such as PLGA, PEG derivatives, chitosan, alginate, and cellulose-based hybrids, which enhance drug stability and enable sustained release profiles. Nano- and microstructured systems, including liposomes, nanoparticles, nanoemulsions, microspheres, and electrospun nanofibers, are discussed for their ability to improve bioavailability and facilitate targeted delivery at the cellular level. Hydrogel-based platforms, particularly injectable and stimuli-responsive systems, are highlighted for their role in localised therapy and tissue engineering applications. Furthermore, the integration of 3D bioprinting technologies enables the fabrication of patient-specific scaffolds and implantable constructs for precision medicine and regenerative therapies. Stimuli-responsive systems, including pH-, temperature-, enzyme-, and externally triggered release platforms, further enhance on-demand drug release in diseased microenvironments. The biomedical applications of CBD-based systems are critically evaluated in antimicrobial therapy, wound healing, tumour-targeted cancer therapy, immunomodulation, microbiome regulation, and regenerative medicine. Finally, this review addresses current translational challenges such as drug loading efficiency, stability issues, scalability, and regulatory barriers, while highlighting future perspectives involving artificial intelligence-guided design, personalised nanomedicine, and advanced biomanufacturing technologies. Overall, CBD-based smart biomaterial platforms represent a highly promising approach for next-generation therapeutic systems with improved efficacy, safety, and clinical potential.

papers.abstract: In situ functionalization of bacterial cellulose (BC) enables the incorporation of compatible functional components during biosynthesis, in contrast to post-synthetic and hybrid modification approaches. BC is produced extracellularly by Komagataeibacter species and has high purity, water-holding capacity, and crystallinity, while its mechanical and biological properties are influenced by production and processing conditions. This narrative review evaluates 78 primary and review articles published between 2005 and 2025. Building on earlier reviews of BC modification, it provides an integrative biochemical, biophysical, and industrial biotechnology perspective on in situ functionalization strategies linking bacterial metabolism and cellulose synthase activity to the incorporation of carbon nanomaterials, conductive polymers, and nanoparticles within the BC matrix. These functionalized nanocomposites often exhibit improved mechanical, thermal, electrical, antimicrobial, and bioactive properties, although additive incorporation may reduce crystallinity depending on concentration, dispersion, and interaction mechanisms. The roles of c-di-GMP signaling, carbon flux regulation, cellulose synthase-directed extrusion, and enzyme-assisted co-assembly in governing material architecture and structure-property relationships are discussed. Key limitations include additive dispersion, bacterial viability, protocol reproducibility, product biocompatibility, and process scale-up. Functionalized BC offers exciting potential as a customizable biofabrication platform for advanced nanomaterials useful in bioelectronics, tissue engineering, wound healing, packaging, and sustainable industrial applications.

papers.title: Extrusion-based bioprinting for functional tissue reconstruction: design strategies and applications.
papers.abstract: Extrusion-based bioprinting has become a widely used biofabrication strategy for tissue engineering because it enables controlled deposition of cell-laden bioinks, biomaterials, and bioactive factors into spatially organized constructs. In this review, we summarize the principles of extrusion-based bioprinting, including major printing configurations, emerging variants, bioink classifications, and key design criteria related to printability, rheology, crosslinking, and post-printing stability. We then discuss recent applications through a function-oriented framework, covering load-bearing structural tissues, barrier and soft connective tissues, contractile tissues, metabolically active parenchymal tissues, vascularized constructs, and neural tissue regeneration. This framework emphasizes that successful bioprinting requires not only anatomical shape reproduction, but also reconstruction of tissue-specific functions, including mechanical support, barrier restoration, vascular perfusion, contractility, metabolic activity, and neural connectivity. We further analyze major challenges, including the trade-off between bioink processability and biological performance, cell viability and structural fidelity, limited multiscale resolution, functional maturation, host integration, and regulatory standardization. papers.title: CHEMICAL VERSUS PHYSICAL SURFACE MODIFICATION OF TITANIUM DENTAL IMPLANTS: A COMPARATIVE REVIEW OF SANDBLASTED, LARGE-GRIT, ACID-ETCHED (SLA) AND FEMTOSECOND LASER-ABLATED SURFACES
papers.abstract: Surface topography governs the rate and quality of osseointegration of titanium dental implants. The sandblasted, large-grit, acid-etched (SLA) surface represents the established chemical-subtractive paradigm and remains the clinical benchmark21[SP1.1], whereas femtosecond (fs) laser ablation has emerged as a physical-subtractive alternative that promises deterministic topographic control, superior surface purity and a thickened, crystalline oxide without the mechanical penalties of acid etching. This review critically compar es the two paradigms across four domains: surface metrology and chemistry, In-vitro biological response, In-vivo biomechanical fixation and histomorphometry, and clinical implications. Evidence indicates that SLA reliably produces a moderately rough (Sa 1–2 µm) surface with high bone-to-implant contact and more than 95% five-year survival, but is constrained by residual alumina embedding, hydrogen-induced embrittlement and stochastic topography. Femtosecond laser processing generates hierarchical micro/nano structures (laser-induced periodic surface structures, LIPSS) with a five-fold thicker oxide, controllable anatase/rutile content, contaminant-free chemistry and markedly enhanced osteoblast adhesion, at the cost of frequently hydrophobic wettability, limited long-term in vivo data and a modest fatigue reduction. The strongest bone-bonding biomechanical data derived from laser-structured (predominantly nanosecond) surfaces, while fs-specific evidence remains largely in vitro and material-scientific. It is concluded that fs-laser ablation is a credible, and in several respects superior, engineering platform whose osteogenic and antibacterial promise is not yet matched by clinical validation. Rational, scenario-based selection guidelines and future directions toward “smart” dual-function surfaces are proposed.

papers.title: Generation wise ranking of PDI core dendrimers for drug encapsulation informed by Gaussian process regression based QSPR analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract In this research, structural interaction analysis of Perylene Diimide (PDI) core dendrimers is conducted over four therapeutic and imaging classes. Core topology was mathematically encoded using topological descriptors, which include Leap Zagreb indices and polymer path Wiener polarity index. Drug generation encapsulation suitability was quantified through global feature normalization and standardized Euclidean distance, yielding compatibility scores used to rank dendrimer generations ( $$D_0$$ - $$D_4$$ ) for each drug without altering drug order or identity. To assess the stability and systematicity of generation suitability trends, intergenerational behavior was evaluated using monotonic rank association via Spearman’s rank correlation and global compatibility magnitude through relative changes in mean compatibility. To determine which topological indices most effectively explain specific physicochemical properties of drugs, that are, molecular weight, surface polarity, hydrogen bonding capacity, rotatable bond flexibility, $$\pi$$ -complexity, and structural intricacy, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) models were developed within a Quantitative Structure-Property Relationship (QSPR) framework using a descriptor space comprising four therapeutic drug-related chemical indices. Model outputs were carefully analysed to evaluate descriptor property relevance using prediction error metrics and correlation statistics, allowing us to determine the most informative and relevant topological index for each chemical attribute. These results demonstrate that the employed topological descriptors provide a systematic graph-based representation for generation wise compatibility and exhibit property-dependent relationships with diverse physicochemical characteristics.

papers.title: Rheological behaviour, structural recovery and printability of customized chocolate inks for extrusion 3D printing
papers.abstract: Background Chocolate ink for extrusion-based 3D food printing requires an optimal balance of rheological behaviour, structural recovery, and textural properties to ensure smooth extrusion, shape retention, and dimensional stability after deposition. This study investigates the influence of the cocoa solids-to-fat ratio on the rheological behaviour, structural recovery, and printability of custom-developed chocolate inks. Methodology Five formulations were prepared by varying cocoa solids (20–28%), cocoa butter (30–34%), and sugar (23.4–35.4%), while keeping the levels of milk powder, palm oil, lecithin, polyglycerol polyricinoleate, and vanilla extract constant. The inks were characterised using steady-state and oscillatory rheological measurements, including flow behaviour, viscoelastic properties, and creep-recovery tests, together with proximate and textural analysis for printability assessment. Results All formulations exhibited shear-thinning behaviour and viscoelastic solid characteristics suitable for extrusion-based 3D printing. The cocoa solids–fat ratio significantly influenced the rheological, textural, and printing properties of the chocolate inks. Formulation containing 22% cocoa powder and 31% cocoa butter achieved the optimal balance of extrusion flowability, structural recovery, texture, and printability, resulting in excellent shape retention. Variations in the cocoa solids–fat ratio also modified the proximate composition, particularly fat and total solids contents, thereby influencing the overall printing performance. Conclusion The cocoa solids–fat ratio is a critical formulation parameter governing the rheological, structural recovery, textural, and printing characteristics of chocolate inks. Optimising this ratio enables the development of chocolate inks with enhanced extrusion performance and dimensional stability, providing practical guidance for designing formulations for extrusion-based 3D food printing applications.

papers.title: A fully Bayesian approach to the generalized hyperbolic process for regression
papers.abstract: This study presents a new and flexible approach to regression modeling called the Generalized Hyperbolic Process for Regression (GHPR), which builds on and extends the well-known Gaussian Process for Regression (GPR). The GHPR is designed to cover a broader range of regression behaviors, with GPR appearing as a special case within this wider framework. A fully Bayesian modeling strategy is used to capture uncertainty and improve prediction. Because the model can be computationally demanding, the analysis focuses on a more efficient weight-space version. To model complex relationships in the data, the approach uses Fourier basis functions, and the Laplace approximation is applied to make inference more tractable. The study also includes theoretical results for both the marginal and predictive distributions. To test how well the model performs, simulations under two scenarios are carried out, and both GHPR and GPR are applied to real data on semiconductor electron mobility. The results show that GHPR consistently provides more accurate predictions.

papers.abstract: Hard point-of-interconnection (POI) export limits can strand otherwise-available photovoltaic (PV) energy unless battery storage is dispatched with sufficient anticipation and under physically consistent constraints.This study evaluates a constraint-audited receding-horizon dispatch framework for curtailment recovery at an anonymized 230 MW utility-scale PV plant with a modeled 195.5 MW export cap and a nominal 30 MW/140 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS).The mixed-integer model predictive controller enforces BESS power and energy limits, charge-discharge exclusivity, no grid charging, forecast-dependent discharge headroom, first-action receding-horizon execution, and a common 50%-to-50% terminal-energy protocol.Twelve rolling monthly folds from September 2024 to August 2025 are evaluated against cap-only operation and a protocol-matched perfect-information Oracle.Cap-only operation curtails 26,279 MWh (4.9872% of evaluated PV energy).A transparent 72 h Diurnal model predictive control (MPC) reduces curtailment to 11,719.454MWh, recovers 14,559.546MWh, and closes 98.450% of the modeled cap-only-to-Oracle recoverable-energy opportunity; the matched Oracle curtails 11,490.175MWh.All 3 h closed-loop trajectories satisfy the modeled export cap, BESS limits, terminal equality, charge-discharge exclusivity, discharge-headroom rule, and no-grid-import condition.A matched information-sensitivity analysis then compares History-CatBoost and Weather-CatBoost under the same controller.Weather-CatBoost lowers daylight mean absolute error (MAE) by 2.225 MW at 24 h and 1.175 MW at 72 h relative to History-CatBoost, while annual curtailment is 288.601MWh higher at 24 h and 99.699 MWh lower at 72 h; the monthly block-bootstrap intervals include zero in both cases.Histogram gradient boosting (HGB) robustness and BESS-sensitivity results further show that the incremental control value of weather information is model-and configuration-dependent.Under the tested plant, cap, BESS, 3 h resolution, horizon, and terminal protocol, physically constrained anticipatory dispatch captures most of the modeled recoverable curtailed energy, leaving comparatively limited residual opportunity for additional forecast sophistication.

papers.title: High‐Precision and High‐Strength Ceramic Micro‐Lattice via Vat Photopolymerization Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Vat photopolymerization enables complex ceramic structures but struggles with precision and mechanical properties. Here, highly reactive ∼150 nm Al 2 O 3 nanopowder with carbon black additive was used to fabricate high‐strength ceramic micro‐lattices. Carbon black reduced light scattering, improving manufacturing precision and achieving ∼14 µm resolution with high shape fidelity. Sintering kinetics were investigated to correlate temperature with relative density and compressive strength of gyroid lattices. Systematic analysis of macro‐/microstructural evolution during sintering revealed that thermal radiation scattering by the highly reactive powder induces an asynchronous sintering between the interior and exterior surfaces, which delays full densification and shifts the peak mechanical performance to a higher temperature. Ultimately, I‐WP micro‐lattices with ∼ 44 µm wall thickness achieved a compressive strength of 103.7 ± 5.31 MPa. By demonstrating outstanding precision, mechanical performance, fine feature size, and small unit cell scale, this work establishes a benchmark for microscale additive manufacturing of ceramic structures, offering insights into both processing optimization and densification mechanisms.

papers.title: Peri‐Infarct Cortical Network Remapping During Stroke Recovery via a Soft Liquid Metal Neural Interface
papers.abstract: Stroke causes substantial reorganization of neural activity and connectivity in the peri-infarct cortex during functional recovery. Tracking these changes at high resolution, however, remains difficult. Mechanical mismatch of conventional rigid neural probes is exacerbated in the fragile peri-infarct region, destabilizing the tissue-electrode interface and limiting long-term recording. Here, we present a fully soft, liquid metal-based multichannel neural interface that enables stable electrophysiological recording in freely moving mice. Using this platform, we performed longitudinal recordings before and after ischemic stroke, enabling within-animal comparisons. We applied complementary analyses of population-level latent dynamics and functional connectivity, capturing network-level coordination and pairwise interactions. Both analyses revealed acute suppression followed by partial recovery without restoration of the pre-stroke state. Instead, neural networks reorganized into a distinct and reproducible functional configuration. These findings establish soft liquid metal neural interfaces combined with population-level analysis as a useful approach for resolving neural reorganization during stroke recovery.

papers.title: A physics-guided residual correction and uncertainty quantification method for interval prediction of combined high- and low-cycle fatigue life under small-sample conditions
papers.abstract: Accurate interval prediction of combined high- and low-cycle fatigue (CCF) life under small-sample conditions remains challenging, as conventional damage models may introduce systematic bias and purely data-driven models may show unstable generalization. This study proposes a physics-guided residual correction and uncertainty quantification method for CCF life interval prediction. The Miner linear damage model is used as a physics-based baseline, and the Miner residual is defined in the logarithmic life domain. Physically informed damage descriptors, including the low-cycle damage ratio, high-cycle damage ratio, life scale ratio, and coupled low–high-cycle damage parameter, are then constructed. Based on these descriptors, a support vector regression (SVR) model is used to learn the Miner residual and correct the physics-based baseline prediction. Residual uncertainty is quantified using the empirical distribution of the remaining prediction residuals, and the 90% prediction interval, 95% prediction interval, and engineering conservative interval (ECI) are constructed using residual quantiles. Thus, point prediction, interval prediction, and empirical safe life estimation are achieved in a unified framework. The method is validated using 43 CCF samples from seven materials through leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). The proposed method achieves an RMSE log 10 of 0.0895. The 95% prediction interval obtains a prediction interval coverage probability of 97.67% with a normalized mean prediction interval width of 0.1123. On the present LOOCV-based validation dataset, the ECI covers all samples, with an error factor of 1.4950. Compared with Miner, Manson–Halford, SVR, and XGBoost, the proposed method provides narrower empirical intervals at comparable coverage levels.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning-based decision-making algorithm for motion sickness mitigation in automated driving
papers.abstract: Automated driving (AD) requires handling multiple coupled objectives, and comfort-oriented decision-making is especially challenging in curved and dynamic traffic environments where motion sickness (MS) is readily induced. Recent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods have demonstrated strong capability in AD planning. Therefore, we propose a hierarchical DRL framework for MS mitigation in AD. The proposed method combines a high-level Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) decision policy with polynomial trajectory generation, model predictive control (MPC)-based trajectory refinement, and LQR/PID tracking control, enabling modular separation of decision-making and control execution. A 9-degree-of-freedom vehicle dynamics model is adopted to capture translational and rotational motion, and the reward function explicitly incorporates Motion Sickness Dose Value (MSDV) together with roll, pitch, and yaw angular rate penalties. The approach is first validated through real-vehicle tests on a drive-by-wire vehicle to establish practical feasibility, and subsequently evaluated in static and dynamic CARLA scenarios. The dynamic-scenario results show that the proposed PPO policy achieves the best comfort performance among the tested learning-based agents, reducing MSDV by 12.16% relative to the sampling-based Lattice baseline. In the dynamic scenario, PPO requires 3.18 ms per decision and achieves a 99.0% collision-free rate. These results confirm that PPO-based comfort trajectory optimization is viable for real-time deployment on autonomous vehicles, and it helps to address the issues of passengers’ acceptance of autonomous driving and driving comfort.
